title: A protocol for the growth and imaging of _in vitro_ attached human embryos
protocol: Remove the cryotube containing the human embryos from the liquid nitrogen.
Place the tube in a 37°C water bath until the content is completely thawed (about 60-90 seconds).
Spray the cryotube with 70% ethanol and gently wipe it clean.
Transfer the contents of the cryotube to an empty 60mm dish using a P1000 pipette.
Identify the embryos under a stereomicroscope and transfer them into ETS1; incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the embryos from ETS1 to ETS2; incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the embryos from ETS2 to ETS3; incubate for 7.5 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the embryos to Cryo-PBS; incubate for 6 minutes at room temperature, then move the dish to a heated surface and incubate for 4 minutes at 37°C.
Visually inspect the embryos for presence or absence of zona pellucida.
Transfer embryos without zona pellucida directly into an ibiTreat µ-plate filled with pre-equilibrated IVC1.
Use a stripper pipette to transfer embryos to minimize carryover of cryo-PBS.
Transfer embryos with zona pellucida directly into an ibiTreat µ-plate filled with pre-equilibrated IVC1.
Transfer one embryo at a time into a droplet of AT solution for zona removal.
Pipette up and down several times in the AT solution to remove the zona pellucida.
Transfer the embryo from the AT solution to a fresh droplet of AT solution.
Repeat step ii until the zona pellucida starts disappearing.
Transfer the embryo without the zona pellucida to a droplet of M2 medium to neutralize the AT solution.
Transfer the embryo to a fresh droplet of M2 medium.
Transfer the embryo to a droplet of IVC1 medium.
Transfer the embryo to a well of an ibiTreat µ-plate filled with pre-equilibrated IVC1.
Dip the pipette tip in IVC1 to wash off traces of mineral oil before final transfer.
Place the ibiTreat µ-plate in the incubator and incubate overnight.
Fill all wells of the µ-plate, including those not containing embryos, with 1xPBS.
Position the µ-plate so that the bottom is not in direct contact with the heated surface of the incubator shelf.
Visually inspect the embryos to assess and record morphology.
Replace half of the media in each well (100 μl) with fresh, pre-equilibrated IVC1 using a stereomicroscope.
Place the ibiTreat µ-plate in the incubator and incubate overnight.
Visually inspect the embryos under a stereomicroscope the next day.
If the embryos are attached, remove half of the media (100 μl) and replace it with 150 μl of pre-equilibrated IVC2.
Do not let the attached embryo(s) dry up.
If embryos have not yet attached, replace half of the media in each well (100 μl) with fresh, pre-equilibrated IVC1.
Place the ibiTreat µ-plate in the incubator.
Incubate overnight.
Replace half of the media in each well with fresh, pre-equilibrated IVC2 every day.
Fix the embryos in 4% PFA in PBS for 30 min at 4°C.
Wash the embryos 3 times for 20 min each in PBS at room temperature.
Quench the embryos in Quench Buffer for 30 min at room temperature.
Block the embryos for 2 h at room temperature.
Stain embryos with primary antibodies diluted in Block Buffer for 5-12 h at room temperature, 3-4 h at 37°C, or overnight at 4°C.
Stain embryos first with antibodies against OCT4 or NANOG to identify normal embryos.
Wash stained embryos at least 3 times for 20 minutes each at room temperature.
Stain embryos with secondary antibodies in Block Buffer for 5-12 hours at room temperature, 3-4 hours at 37°C, or overnight at 4°C.
Incubate embryos with DAPI for 5-12 hours at room temperature, 3-4 hours at 37°C, or overnight at 4°C.
Incubate embryos with Phalloidin for 5-12 hours at room temperature, 3-4 hours at 37°C, or overnight at 4°C.
Image stained embryos immediately after staining with Phalloidin and brief washes to remove excess.
Image embryos attached to the bottom of the ibiTreat µ-plate in Wash Buffer using an inverted confocal microscope.
Adjust laser intensity and/or gain as needed.
Use high NA air or water immersion objectives (20x-40x).
Ensure images are at least 12 bits/pixel with a resolution of 1024x1024 pixels.
Apply line averaging as necessary, at least 2x.
Consider using a white light laser (WLL) for optimal excitation wavelengths.
Tailor emission windows to maximize signal and minimize potential cross-talk.
Use typical excitation/emission settings for DAPI: 405 diode laser/ 415-486.
Adjust WLL settings for Alexa 488, 555, and 647 as appropriate.
When adding Alexa 594, adjust the setting for Alexa 555 to 560-580.
Add a fifth track at WLL 594/602-631 if using Alexa 594.
Use the recommended Nyquist z-interval for best resolution.
Consider intervals slightly larger than Nyquist, but smaller than optical section thickness.
Establish intensity correction curves for each channel before imaging.
Start with DAPI and image from the bottom to the top of the embryo.
Progressively increase laser power from 0.1% to 100% as needed to maintain constant DAPI signal.
Increase gains if necessary, typically no more than 20% to avoid noise.
Save and apply the correction curve during image acquisition.
Repeat for all channels using the shape of the DAPI curve as a general guide.
Deconvolve images using Autoquant’s 3D blind deconvolution algorithm for 10 iterations with default parameters.
Export final images to 16-bit floating point tiffs.
Import deconvolved tiff files into Imaris.
Check the image properties to ensure x, y, z dimensions are read appropriately from the metadata on import and adjust if necessary.
Explore data in Imaris’ 3D mode to reveal 3D tissue organization of cell lineages.
Segment cells in 3D using spot finding or surface algorithms as appropriate with parameters determined from size and signal-to-noise threshold of features of interest.
Export movies for 3D display.
Set rendering quality to the highest level ("1").
Use 24 frames per second (fps) for export.
Do not apply compression during export.
Export in high definition format.
